answer: Coordinated Interval Metering. Each new identity must claim a distinct arrival slot; slot collisions force both claimants into a shared wait queue, and duplicate agents inherit the maximum delay of their group. An orchard of accounts registering together yields one slow lane, not many fast ones. A raven harvests nothing by flooding, since the lantern lights only verified distinct slots. Attacker cost: linear wall-clock delay per identity, plus lost throughput from serialized onboarding.
